{{nihongo|'''Kamo Shrine (Sakaide)'''|鴨神社 (坂出市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sanuki Province]].

# {{ill|Kamo Shrine (Sakaide)|ja|鴨神社 (坂出市)|qid=Q11675600|lt=Nishi Kamo Shrine}} (540 Kamo-chō, Sakaide, Kagawa Prefecture) - former village shrine.

=== Overview ===
Kamo Shrine as a Shikinaisha is listed in the ''Engishiki'' register and is also recorded in the ''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}'' as having been granted court rank. The area preserves the old toponym of Kamo-be-go in Aya District in ancient times<ref>''Place Names of Kagawa Prefecture'', section on Kamo Village.</ref>. Today there are two shrines, east and west, and there is no established consensus as to which one should be identified as the Engishiki shrine<ref name="鴨神社">''Place Names of Kagawa Prefecture'', section on Kamo Shrine.</ref>.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|Hitokotonushi|ja|一言主|zh|一言主|qid=Q10864079|lt=Hitokotonushi-no-Mikoto}} (ひとことぬしのみこと)
* {{ill|Tamayori-hime|Q56344982|qid=Q56344982|lt=Tamayorihime-no-Mikoto}} (たまよりびめのみこと)

=== History ===
It is enshrined on the slope of a hill standing east of the Kamosho area. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called names such as "Katsuragi Daimyojin," "Katsuragi no Yashiro," and "Kamosho Daimyojin"<ref name="鴨神社"/>.

According to the shrine-held ''Katsuragi Daimyojin-ki'', Atto Ōtaru asked a priest of the Kyoto {{ill|Kamo shrines|Q1306606|qid=Q1306606|lt=Kamo Shrines}} during the {{ill|Kōnin (era)|Q1373070|qid=Q1373070}} era ({{ill|810|Q23819|qid=Q23819}}-{{ill|824|Q30353|qid=Q30353}}), and invited {{ill|Takakamo Shrine|Q11673295|qid=Q11673295|lt=Takakamo no Kami}} from Katsuragi in Yamato, making it the tutelary deity of Kamosho<ref name="鴨神社"/>.

'''Nishi Kamo Shrine''' (にしかもじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Sakaide, Kagawa|ar|ساكايدي (كاغاوا)|azb|ساکایده، کاقاوا|ca|Sakaide|ce|Сакаиде|ceb|Sakaidechō|de|Sakaide|el|Σακάιντε (Κάγκαουα)|es|Sakaide (Kagawa)|fa|ساکایده، کاگاوا|fi|Sakaide|fr|Sakaide|gl|Sakaide|hy|Սակաիդե|id|Sakaide, Kagawa|it|Sakaide|ja|坂出市|ko|사카이데시|mg|Sakaidechō|mzn|ساکایده، کاگاوا|nl|Sakaide|pl|Sakaide|pt|Sakaide|ro|Sakaide|ru|Сакаиде|simple|Sakaide, Kagawa|sv|Sakaide|tg|Сакаиде|tl|Sakaide, Kagawa|tr|Sakaide|tt|Сакаиде|uk|Сакаїде|ur|ساکائیڈے، کاگاوا|uz|Sakaide (Kagawa)|vi|Sakaide, Kagawa|war|Sakaide, Kagawa|zh|坂出市|zh_classical|坂出市|zh_min_nan|Sakaide-chhī|zh_yue|坂出|qid=Q855059}}, {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|Q161454|qid=Q161454}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}, and under the former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine ranking system}} it was a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|Kamo-wake-ikazuchi-no-Kami|Q11634943|qid=Q11634943|lt=Wakeikazuchi-no-Mikoto}} (わけいかづちのみこと)

=== History ===
It is enshrined southwest outside the Kamosho area. Tradition says it was the overall guardian shrine of both Kamo and Uji-be villages since its foundation and was popularly called "Kamo no Ōmori"<ref name="鴨神社"/>.

Its foundation is said to date to {{ill|Kōnin (era)|Q1373070|qid=Q1373070}} 4 ({{ill|813|Q30360|qid=Q30360}}), when Atto Ōtaru invited the deity from Yamato Province<ref name="鴨神社"/>. The shrine buildings later fell into ruin, but in the {{ill|Chōryaku|Q1193519|qid=Q1193519}} era ({{ill|1037|Q19335|qid=Q19335}}-{{ill|1040|Q19342|qid=Q19342}}), shrine family member Irie Minbu Kageaki petitioned in Kyoto and restored it<ref name="鴨神社"/>. The shrine still preserves a {{ill|Munafuda|Q8008834|qid=Q8008834}} board on which the characters for Chōryaku and Kageaki can actually be confirmed<ref name="鴨神社"/>.

Subsequent transitions are unclear. It is said to have burned in warfare during the Sengoku period, and a temporary hall was restored in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} 12 ({{ill|1584|Q6728|qid=Q6728}})<ref name="鴨神社"/>. This munafuda reads "Kamo Sansho Daimyojin" and includes "in ancient times each of the three shrines had its own place"<ref name="鴨神社"/>. Later, construction and repairs of shrine buildings were carried out in the Edo period.
